overview: A fan-out (multicast) implementation of ZoomVideoSDKDelegate. The Zoom Video SDK exposes a single delegate slot; this class occupies that slot and re-broadcasts every callback it receives to a set of weakly-held child delegates, enabling many observers to listen to SDK events simultaneously. Exposed publicly as ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate. The public API is intentionally tiny: init(), add(_:), remove(_:); the dozens of ZoomVideoSDKDelegate methods are conformance plumbing, not APIs to call directly.
keyCharacteristics: Single registration target: the toolkit assigns one instance to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate (via ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize) and exposes it as ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.
Weak child storage via NSHashTable.weakObjects(); the composite holds children weakly and automatically removes deallocated ones.

Optional-callback forwarding: every ZoomVideoSDKDelegate method is optional; the composite forwards each via optional chaining ($0.onSomething?(...)), so a child only receives callbacks it implements.
Synchronous fan-out: iterates delegates.allObjects and invokes each registered child; stateless; returns nothing to the SDK from the fan-out.

typeDefinitions.name: ZoomVideoSDKDelegate
typeDefinitions.notes: The protocol the composite conforms to and that child delegates must conform to. All methods are optional.

typeDefinitions.name: NSHashTable<AnyObject>
typeDefinitions.notes: Configured via .weakObjects() for zeroing weak references and pointer-identity dedup. Backs the child store.

typeDefinitions.name: ZMUIToolKitManager
typeDefinitions.role: owns the shared instance as static let videoSDKDelegate; assigns it to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate in initialize

typeDefinitions.name: ZoomVideoSDK
typeDefinitions.notes: Exposes a single delegate slot occupied by the composite.

prerequisites: A single instance is created and owned by the toolkit as ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate (a static let). Integrators normally do NOT construct their own instance.

The instance becomes live (begins receiving SDK callbacks) only after ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize(videoSDK:bundleId:) runs, because that method assigns videoSDK.delegate = videoSDKDelegate. Before initialization, registered children receive nothing because the SDK has no delegate wired to the composite.

entryPoints.note: From this point, SDK callbacks fan out to all registered children.

actions: clears ZoomVideoSDK.delegate if toolkit still owns the slot (sdk.delegate === videoSDKDelegate)
exitPoints.note: Registered child delegates are KEPT in the composite's weak table so listeners persist across SDK re-initialization. The composite itself is a static let and lives for the process lifetime.

registrationModel.guidance: Always register through the composite rather than assigning directly to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate; the toolkit owns that slot, and registering here keeps every toolkit component connected. Use add(_:)/remove(_:).

memorySemantics.summary: The memory contract of the class.
points: Children are held weakly. Each child is held by a weak (zeroing) reference.

The caller owns the child's lifetime. Retain your observer for as long as you want it to receive callbacks. If the only strong reference is dropped, the object is deallocated and removed from the table, and its callbacks stop.
No retain cycles: because storage is weak, registering does not create a retain cycle between the composite and its children. This is why toolkit views can add(self) in init without leaking.
remove(_:) in deinit is optional: a deallocated child is automatically removed from the weak table. Calling remove(_:) in deinit provides deterministic cleanup but is not required.
Duplicate adds are deduplicated by NSHashTable.weakObjects() using object pointer identity, so adding the same instance twice produces a single entry and a single delivery.

threading.deliveryThread: the thread the SDK invokes (typically main)
points: Callbacks are delivered to registered observers on the thread the SDK invokes. Each callback method calls forward { ... }, which iterates and invokes children on that thread.
In practice the Zoom Video SDK delivers ZoomVideoSDKDelegate callbacks on the main thread, so children typically receive them on main.
Guidance for children: Register and remove observers on the main thread, and dispatch to the main thread inside your observer if you update UI. Keep callback handlers fast.

apis.name: init
apis.description: Default initializer. Calls super.init() and creates an empty weak child table. Integrators normally do not call this; they use the shared ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate instance.
apis.returns: an empty composite with no registered children

apis.name: add
apis.description: Registers a child delegate to receive forwarded SDK callbacks. The child is stored weakly.

parameters.name: delegate
parameters.description: An object conforming to ZoomVideoSDKDelegate. Implement only the optional methods you care about.

preconditions: Call from the main thread (consistent with ZMUIToolKitManager usage).
sideEffects: Adds delegate to the weak hash table. Adding the same object more than once results in a single entry (pointer-identity dedup).
apis.memory: The composite holds delegate weakly. The caller must keep a strong reference for as long as callbacks are needed.

apis.name: remove
apis.description: Unregisters a previously-added child delegate so it stops receiving forwarded callbacks.

parameters.name: delegate
parameters.description: The object previously passed to add(_:).

sideEffects: Removes delegate from the weak hash table. Removing an object that was never added (or already removed/deallocated) has no effect.

apis.name: forward
apis.description: Internal fan-out helper. Iterates delegates.allObjects, casts each entry to ZoomVideoSDKDelegate, and invokes block for it. Every public ZoomVideoSDKDelegate method on the composite delegates to this. Documented for completeness; not part of the public API surface.

parameters.name: block
parameters.description: Closure invoked once per registered child.

sideEffects: Invokes block synchronously for each registered child in allObjects iteration order.

forwardingContract.description: Universal forwarding contract for every callback the composite implements.
forwardingContract.thread: delivered on the thread the SDK invokes (typically main)
forwardingContract.delivery: synchronous, to each registered child that implements the optional method
forwardingContract.optionalChaining: forwarded via $0.onSomething?(...) so only children implementing the method receive it

errorHandling.description: CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate does not produce or interpret errors. It is a pure relay.
points: add(_:) and remove(_:) never fail and never throw. Duplicate adds and unknown removes have no effect.

Error-bearing SDK callbacks (e.g. onError(_:detail:), onFailed(toStartShare:user:), subscribe-fail callbacks) are forwarded verbatim to children. Interpreting and recovering from those errors is each child's responsibility.
Because fan-out is synchronous, keep callback handlers fast.

required: Register observers via ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:) (Obj-C addDelegate:). Unregister with remove(_:) (Obj-C removeDelegate:).
Keep a strong reference to any observer you register; the composite holds children weakly.
Call ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize(videoSDK:bundleId:) so the composite is wired to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate; otherwise registered children receive nothing.
Register and remove observers on the main thread, and dispatch to the main thread inside your observer if you update UI.
guidance: Always register through the composite rather than assigning directly to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate. The toolkit owns that slot; registering here keeps every toolkit component connected.
Keep forwarded callback handlers fast, since fan-out is synchronous.

codeSnippets.name: mainThreadSafeCallback
codeSnippets.description: Callbacks are forwarded on the SDK's calling thread (usually main, not guaranteed). Dispatch to main before touching UIKit.

codeSnippets.aiHint: Use the composite as a direct callback relay, and dispatch to the main thread in your observer when updating UIKit.
